subject: Archaeology
title: Iraq's Archaeologists Rebuilding Heritage
description: A quick, practical guide to Iraq's Archaeologists Rebuilding Heritage.

hook.text: While the world mourned Iraq's lost heritage, Iraqi archaeologists quietly kept working — often at great personal risk.

buildup.text: During years of conflict, Iraqi scholars hid artifacts, buried records, and sandbagged museum displays to protect them.

discovery.text: After ISIS was driven out, Iraqi and international teams found that sandbagging and quick burials had saved many treasures.

twist.text: Iraq has more unexcavated sites than any country on earth. Decades of war have delayed research but not destroyed the resolve.

climax.text: A new generation of Iraqi archaeologists is training abroad and returning. They are determined to tell their own story.

punchline.text: The cradle of civilization is broken but not empty.

quiz.question: How did Iraqi archaeologists protect artifacts during conflict?
options: They shipped everything to museums in neighboring countries
They hid artifacts, buried records, and sandbagged museum displays
They digitized everything and destroyed the originals to prevent looting
